findings.criterion: `_rate_for()` returns the numeric rate and a bounded source value.
findings.detail: handler.py lines 227-275: `_rate_for()` still has return type `-> float` and returns bare floats at lines 264, 268, 272, and 275. No tuple, named-tuple, or dataclass with a source label is returned.

findings.criterion: `_rate_for()` labels exact empirical matches as `empirical`.
findings.detail: handler.py line 264: `return exact` — returns a bare float with no `empirical` label.

findings.criterion: `_rate_for()` labels seed matches as `seed`.
findings.detail: handler.py line 268: `return seed` — returns a bare float with no `seed` label.

findings.criterion: `_rate_for()` labels input-derived empirical matches as `empirical_scaled`.
findings.detail: handler.py line 272: `return base * mult` — returns a bare float with no `empirical_scaled` label.

findings.criterion: `_rate_for()` labels `UNKNOWN_RATE_PER_1K` fallback matches as `fallback`.
findings.detail: handler.py line 275: `return UNKNOWN_RATE_PER_1K * mult` — returns a bare float with no `fallback` label.

findings.criterion: Every `_rate_for()` call site in `handler.py` is updated to the new return contract.
findings.detail: handler.py line 365: `total += units_1k * _rate_for(model_id, metric_name, rates)` — still treats `_rate_for()` as returning a bare float. No unpacking of a (rate, source) result.

findings.criterion: `MeteredSpend` carries the estimated-provenance flag as a field alongside `degraded` and `failures`.
findings.detail: handler.py lines 287-291: `MeteredSpend` has only `total`, `degraded`, and `failures` fields. No `estimated` (or `metered_estimated`) field is present.

findings.criterion: `_metered_spend()` reports estimated provenance when any component source is `seed`.
findings.detail: handler.py lines 365-371: No provenance accumulator exists. `_rate_for()` returns a bare float with no source label, so there is no way to detect `seed` sources. `MeteredSpend` has no `estimated` field.

findings.criterion: `_metered_spend()` reports estimated provenance when any component source is `fallback`.
findings.detail: handler.py lines 365-371: No provenance accumulator exists. `_rate_for()` returns a bare float with no source label, so there is no way to detect `fallback` sources. `MeteredSpend` has no `estimated` field.

findings.criterion: `_metered_spend()` reports estimated provenance as false when every component source is `empirical` or `empirical_scaled`.
findings.detail: handler.py lines 287-291 and 371: `MeteredSpend` has no `estimated` field. No logic exists to report estimated provenance as false for empirical/empirical_scaled sources.

data.remediation: How to resolve the unmet criteria: use the evidence path that matches each one. For codebase-verifiable work, complete any unfinished work and make its proof discoverable in the repository. For evidence that inherently lives outside the repository, mark the criterion with the exact `[non-codebase]` tag and add a comment to this ticket that documents the concrete artifacts that meet it (commands and their output, links, or the reasoning that ties the evidence to the criterion). The completion verifier reads this ticket's comments, so properly tagged evidence you record there is taken into account on the next verification. An untagged external criterion cannot be satisfied by a ticket comment alone. Then re-verify. Note that a finding reporting a ticket record as absent means it was NOT VISIBLE IN THE TICKET SNAPSHOT THE VERIFIER READ — that snapshot is pinned when the run starts, so a record written after the pin, or not yet committed to the store, reads as missing even though it exists; re-verify after the write lands rather than re-recording evidence you already wrote.
